newsitem.title: UK: Allied Colloids sets US buy, rights issue.
newsitem.headline: Allied Colloids sets US buy, rights issue.

text.p: British chemicals company Allied Colloids Plc said on Tuesday it planned to buy CPS Chemical Company Inc for $390 million and alongside it set a two-for-seven rights issue at 118p per share to raise about 173 million stg net.
In a statement Allied Colloids, which also announced first-half results, said CPS made chemical intermediates and finished polymer products for industrial use.
"CPS's activities are linked to Allied Colloids' core chemistry and it has been a supplier to Allied Colloids for the last seven years," the Yorkshire-based company said.
Allied Colloids said the rights issue has been fully underwritten by Kleinwort Benson. HSBC James Capel are acting as brokers. The balance of the cost of CPS will be funded from bank facilities.

In 1995 CPS, which has operations in New Jersey and Arkansas, made pre-tax profits of $35.5 million on sales of $157.0 million. Allied Colloids said the acquisition would give it increased exposure to its core market and a leading position in the U.S. for high value intermediates used in water-soluble polymers.

Allied said it expected the acquisition to be earnings enhancing in its first full financial year, and to lead to substantial tax benefits. It said the acquisition should result in around $345 million of goodwill for U.S. federal income tax purposes.
On a pro-forma basis the enlarged group had net gearing of just under 61 percent as of Nov 1.
Allied Colloids said it expected to have net gearing of 53 percent by March 31, 1997, "with strong interest cover, and gearing to fall steadily thereafter."
